facts.text: Ketchum was originally called Leadville in 1880, renamed after trapper David Ketchum when the postal service found the name too common.
In the 1880s, the Philadelphia Smelter on Warm Springs Road processed lead and silver for a decade, making Ketchum a smelting hub.
By 1920, Ketchum became the largest sheep‑shipping center in the West, with summer flocks grazing in nearby mountains.
After Sun Valley’s 1936 development, Ernest Hemingway and Gary Cooper frequented Ketchum, and Hemingway even bought a home overlooking the Big Wood River in the 1950s.
Clint Eastwood’s 1985 film Pale Rider was partially shot in the Boulder Mountains near Ketchum.
Every Labor Day weekend, Ketchum hosts Wagon Days, a carnival featuring Old‑West wagon trains, ore wagons, and a parade.
